boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Trinity study environments, spanning library seating, specialized collections, academic-building lobbies, and a café-style commons.

cards.entity_name: Raether Library and Information Technology Center
cards.title: Raether Library & Information Technology Center
cards.subtitle: Main library and technology center
cards.notes: Start at the Library & IT Desk on Level A, then choose a library seat for reading, research, or computer-based coursework.
cards.short_summary: Trinity’s main library and technology hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s Library & Information Technology Services is based in the Raether Library & Information Technology Center and supports research and learning needs.
cards.access_notes: During regular semesters, Trinity community access is listed as Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–1 a.m., Friday 8 a.m.–8 p.m., Saturday noon–8 p.m., and Sunday noon–1 a.m.; verify exceptions on the hours page.

cards.title: Level 2 Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Raether Library & Information Technology Center
cards.notes: Use a study cubby in the Level 2 reading room when you want a library-based individual work setting.
cards.short_summary: Library reading-room cubbies for focused work.
cards.evidence_claim: A Trinity admissions article identifies study cubbies in the Level 2 reading room in the library as a campus study setting.
cards.access_notes: Located in the library; use the current library building-access schedule and observe posted room rules.

cards.title: Raether Library 24-Hour Zone
cards.subtitle: South side of the Raether Library building
cards.notes: Bring your current Trinity ID and use the south-side 24-hour zone when the rest of the building’s schedule is more limited.
cards.short_summary: ID-access study space available around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity states that 24-hour-zone spaces on the south side of the library building are available to people with a current Trinity ID.
cards.access_notes: Current Trinity ID required; the hours page says these south-side spaces are available 24 hours, including when holiday building access is otherwise limited.

cards.title: Watkinson Library
cards.subtitle: Main level, Raether Library & Information Technology Center
cards.notes: Schedule an appointment if you need a research session with rare books, manuscripts, art, music, or archival materials.
cards.short_summary: Special-collections research setting inside the LITC.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watkinson is Trinity’s specialized research library for rare books, historic collections, manuscripts, art, music, ephemera, and photography.
cards.source_title: The Watkinson Library: Bringing Rare Books and Special Collections to Life
cards.access_notes: The current LITS hours page lists Watkinson visits Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–noon and 1:30–4 p.m., by appointment only.

cards.title: Chemistry Library
cards.subtitle: Clement Chemistry Building
cards.notes: Set up in the Chemistry Library for quiet work, and look for its documented balcony spaces before settling into a longer session.
cards.short_summary: Quiet subject-library space with balcony areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes the Chemistry Library as a quiet study spot with balcony spaces; it is located in the Clement Chemistry Building.
cards.access_notes: Located in Clement Chemistry Building; confirm building access and any department-specific rules before arrival.

cards.title: Economics Library
cards.subtitle: Trinity College campus
cards.notes: Use the Economics Library as a quiet alternative when you need to step away from the main library for independent reading or writing.
cards.short_summary: A documented quiet alternative to the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s admissions site identifies the Economics Library as a quiet campus study spot.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the library’s current location, building access, and any department-specific rules before arrival.

cards.title: Austin Arts Center Lobby
cards.subtitle: Near Peter B’s
cards.notes: Use the lobby’s large front doors and natural light for a change of setting; keep your materials compact around arts-center traffic.
cards.short_summary: Naturally lit lobby workspace near Peter B’s.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes the Austin Arts lobby as a campus study alternative with large front doors that let in natural light.
cards.access_notes: Lobby use is subject to building access and events; check posted notices when you arrive.

cards.entity_name: Crescent Center for Arts and Neuroscience Lobby
cards.title: Crescent Center for Arts and Neuroscience Lobby
cards.subtitle: CCAN, Trinity College campus
cards.notes: Choose a lobby seat between classes, especially when your schedule already has you near Crescent Street and the science quad.
cards.short_summary: Windowed campus lobby for between-class study.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies the Crescent Center for Arts and Neuroscience lobby as a study space, particularly useful near Crescent Street and the Life Science Center quad.
cards.access_notes: Lobby use is subject to building access and classes or events taking place nearby.

cards.title: Life Science Center Lobby
cards.subtitle: LSC, Trinity College campus
cards.notes: Use the lobby for a focused stretch between science-quad classes, then move on if class transitions make the area active.
cards.short_summary: Campus-lobby study space by the science quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies the Life Science Center lobby as a study space and notes its proximity to the LSC quad.
cards.access_notes: Lobby use is subject to building access and class activity before and after scheduled sessions.

cards.title: Dangremond Family Commons
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to McCook and Hallden Halls
cards.notes: Use this café-style commons for individual work or a small meeting when it is not reserved for a campus event.
cards.short_summary: Open café-style study and meeting commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity states that Dangremond Family Commons is an open, café-style study and meeting space for faculty and students outside scheduled events.
cards.source_title: Center for Teaching and Learning: About Us
cards.access_notes: Located adjacent to McCook and Hallden Halls; campus groups may book it for Common Hour events, so check for event use before settling in.
